What Kaavalan note protects, and what it does not. Read once before relying on it for sensitive data.
Your notes never leave this device
The notes, people, and instructions you save live in a local database on this phone. There is no cloud sync, no account, no server. The app does not phone home.
The vault is encrypted on disk
The local database is encrypted with SQLCipher. If this phone is seized while locked, the database file is unreadable without the device\'s screen-lock key.
If the device is seized while unlocked
Treat the data as compromised. The running app can read the encrypted database. This is the same boundary every secure messaging app draws; there is no defence against an unlocked-device adversary.

Backup files are encrypted with a key derived from your recovery phrase. So the daily backup can run without asking you every time, a copy of that key is kept in encrypted app storage on this device — the backups are not protected by your memory alone. Restoring on a new device still needs the phrase; lose it and you lose the backups.
The Hidden vault is a UI filter

Hidden mode hides selected items from the home list. A forensic adversary with access to the database file can still see that a hidden mode exists. This is behavioural concealment, not cryptographic deniability. For true deniability, the database itself would need to be encrypted twice with two different keys.

A short explanation of what makes Kaavalan note different.
Every byte of your data lives on this device, in a SQLCipher-encrypted database. There is no cloud sync, no analytics, no telemetry. A thief who pulls the SD card cannot read your notes.

Notes are tied to a person (your SP, your SHO, a witness). Tap a person to see everything you ever gave them or took from them. Decay reminders nudge you to follow up with people you have not touched in 30 / 60 / 90 days.

A 6-digit vault PIN hides sensitive notes from the list. A 24-word recovery phrase is the only way back in if you forget the PIN. Write the recovery phrase on paper and store the paper somewhere physically safe.
Kaavalan note is private, local-only software. No ads, no premium tier, no tracking. The full source is on GitHub if you want to read the threat model or audit the crypto.
